why: Greedy with a heap of the best so far: ropes should cover the biggest climbs seen so far. Keep a min-heap of the climbs currently assigned a rope; when there are more climbs than ropes, the smallest one is paid with sandbags instead.
hints: A rope is worth the most on a big climb, sandbags are best spent on small ones. But you only see climbs as you go: how can you keep your options open?
Tentatively give every climb a rope. When you have used one more rope than you own, take back the rope from the smallest climb so far and pay that climb with sandbags.
Min-heap of climbs; push each positive d; if len(heap) > ropes, sandbags -= heappop(heap); if sandbags < 0, return i. Otherwise return n-1. O(n log ropes).
pitfalls: Downhill or flat moves are free and must not enter the heap.
Return the index you are standing on (i), not i+1, when you cannot pay for the move to i+1.
